entry.dc:title: Application of a rock buttress in the design of slopes of a strip coal mine adjacent to a highway
entry.dc:creator: Ulusay R.
entry.dc:description: Eskihisar open pit mine, located at Yatagan, southwest Turkey, produces thermal coal for a power generating plant. As mining of strips advanced southwards, instability appeared to be highly critical due to the movements in the southeast wall slopes adjacent to the state highway running parallel to the pit boundary. This situation called for an immediate response to initiate a detailed geotechnical investigation program and to redesign the pit slopes. This paper outlines the most probable mode and mechanism of instability along the southeast wall, as well as field and laboratory studies, results of back analysis, discussion of the data requirements, and results of slope stability analyses performed to ensure adequate overall stability. -from Authors

entry.dc:title: The Warta Glaciation (stage) within the Widawka drainage basin and the Belchatow opencast
entry.dc:creator: Baraniecka M.
entry.dc:description: The Warta drainage basin, especially the Widawka part, is the stratotype region for the cold Warta stage. Deposits exposed at the Belchatow open pit mine as well as recognized in the entire region gave an opportunity to determine following sequence: from ice-sheet transgression, from glaciation (three till horizons dated at 183 000, 179 000 and 150 00 yr BP) and from recession. A vast literature and numerous results of investigations carried out at the opencast helped to place the Warta-age sediments in complete Quaternary profile. The Lublin Interglacial (an equivalent of the oxygen isotope stage 7) confines the Warta unit from the bottom; the Eemian deposits from the top. The Warta state belongs to the Middle Polish Glaciation "Superstage' (Saalian). There is an extended English summary. -from English summary

entry.dc:title: The lihir gold project; Process plant design
entry.dc:creator: Ketcham V.J.
entry.dc:description: The Lihir deposit in Papua New Guinea (PNG) contains an estimated mineable reserve of 13.7 million ounces of gold in refractory sulphide ore. RTZ, through its subsidiary Kennecott Corporation and in joint venture with Niugini Mining Limited, has submitted a conditional proposal to the PNG government to develop an open pit mine and to install a process plant and associated infrastructure facilities on Lihir Island. The process plant, which will employ Sherritt Gordon pressure oxidation technology, has a design capacity of 2.825 Mt/a of ore containing 7.2% sulphide sulphur. On the basis of its sulphur capacity, the Lihir plant would be one of the largest pressure oxidation facilities in the world. An extensive programme of process development testwork and feasibility engineering was completed to establish the process plant design for the Lihir Project. Efforts have been directed at improving project viability in the face of a deteriorating gold price. Summary results of laboratory and pilot plant testwork on Lihir ore are presented. Key design criteria, a summary flowsheet, and major equipment selected for the commercial plant are also presented and discussed. © 1993.

entry.dc:title: Transportation and port facilities for new mines
entry.dc:creator: Zonailo G.
entry.dc:description: An overview of planning, environmental, and operational considerations involved in developing transportation systems and bulk terminal facilities for new mine developments. Example given include the Escondida copper project in Chile; the La Loma coal project in Colombia; the Socuy open pit mine; and the Westshore and Ridley coal export terminals in Canada. These examples illustrate the pre-planning and progressive development that occurs after transportation, infrastructure and port facilities have been developed. (J.M.McLaughlin)

entry.dc:title: Working conditions and sanitation measures during the pilot-plant exploitation of the continuous operating complex in KATEK coal open pit mine
entry.dc:creator: Borisenkova R.V.
entry.dc:description: Working conditions were analysed in workers engaged into realization of the new coal extracting line technology producing 5250 m<sup>3</sup> of coal per hr in KATEK coal open pit. Hygienic standards appeared to be followed mainly on the constant working places and in the mining machine cabs, but noise dust parameters were not evaluated in the transloaders, microclimate parameters of excavator and transloaders were not assessed during the cold season. High concentration of dust appeared in the air due to mining machines cleaning with the pumped air. Workers engaged into the coal transportation and its intermediate storage appeared to work in more hazardous conditions. Sanitary measures are suggested.

entry.dc:title: Mountain restoration: Soil and surface wildlife habitat
entry.dc:creator: MacCullum B.
entry.dc:description: Much wildlife habitat is being destroyed by extractive resource industries in mountain environments. This article illustrates how mountain wildlife habitat was restored in a devastated area. A strip mine for coal on the east slopes of the Alberta Rockies, occupied during its operations by Rocky Mountain bighorn sheep (Ovis canadensis canadensis, Shaw 1803), was reclaimed as bighorn habitat. By considering the behaviour and habitat requirements of bighorns in conjunction with an operating coal mine and reclamation process, a large coal mining company has been able to reconstruct the mine site restoration to benefit mountain sheep. Although bighorn habitat requirements are well known, it was not until the animal and its requirements were studied against the backdrop of an operating coal mine that obvious recommendations regarding the maintenance and placement of high steep excavated rock faces were made and accepted by the government regulatory agencies. An open pit mine is a devastated landscape; trees, soil and overburden are removed to retrieve coal that may be up to 215 m underground. Overburden and soil are returned, but the disturbance compares to the barren landscapes left behind by glaciers. Contouring of the land, grading of overburden and soil, seeding with grass and legume mixtures and extensive fertilization are designed to speed plant colonization and soil development. By examining the bighorn's biological needs with respect to specific mining operations, a unique opportunity arose to employ McHarg's "design with nature" concept. This approach incorporates environmental and societal values into every aspect of development, and promotes the evaluation of the constraints and opportunities arising. The sheep numbered about 200. Their seasonal movements were similar to those found on native ranges. They used the reclaimed areas as winter range and for the mineral licks exposed during mining; in summer, the sheep moved to nearby alpine areas. Two thirds of all sightings were confined to 1.3 km<sup>2</sup> of reclaimed grassland; its average productivity (4190 kg/ha) exceeded native ranges (1700 kg/ha). The body mass of female sheep in autumn equalled that of the largest in Alberta, but the skull dimensions were not larger than those of adjacent ranges. Infestation with lungworms was moderate. Lamb production and survival were high. Design criteria should be: feeding areas should be dry and lie within 300 m of escape terrain, which should have a slope of 40% and contain at least three benches. Rock piles should be placed on grazing areas. Mineral licks, a vital welfare factor, already existed within the high walls created by strip mining. © 1992 Kluwer Academic Publishers.

entry.dc:title: Hydrogeological Decision Analysis: 3. Application to Design of a Ground‐Water Control System at an Open Pit Mine
entry.dc:creator: Sperling T.
entry.dc:description: Control of ground water plays an important part in operations at many open pit mines. Selection of an efficient and cost‐effective ground‐water control program is frequently complicated by the complex and somewhat uncertain hydrogeo‐logic environment found at most mine sites. This paper documents a case study of dewatering operations at Highland Valley Copper that shows how risk‐cost‐benefit analysis can be used to identify the best ground‐water control strategy to improve stability of pit walls under such conditions. For each of a specified set of design alternatives, the analysis involves evaluation of an economic objective function, comprised of revenues, operating costs, and monetary risks associated with slope failure. The risk calculation requires an accurate estimate of the probability of slope failure on the pit wall. The calculation involves a coupled, steady‐state, saturated‐unsaturated, finite‐element ground‐water flow model and a limit equilibrium slope stability model. The coupled model is invoked in a conditional Monte Carlo simulation that is based on a geostatistical description of the level of uncertainty inherent in the available hydrogeological and geotechnical data. Although the emphasis in this paper is on identifying the optimum slope angle and ground‐water control strategy for open pit mines, the framework is equally well‐suited to the analysis of design issues for any engineering projects in which the hydrogeological environment plays an important role. entry.dc:title: Dragline loading analysis in marine sediment areas of the Syncrude open pit mine
entry.dc:creator: List B.
entry.dc:description: Draglines are use to excavate ore from atop an operating bench at the Syncrude Canada Ltd, the world's largest oil sand mine operator. Failure of the highwall slope along thin marine clay layers can cause danger and impede productivity of the draglines. Geotechnical investigations were made to better understand the failure mechanisms and thus reduce the negative impact on the dragline production. Optimization of productivity and safety assurance are given emphasis.

entry.dc:title: Single hole test blasting at an open pit mine in full scale: A case study
entry.dc:creator: Bilgin H.A.
entry.prism:publicationName: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
entry.dc:description: A study by a series of single hole blasts, slab blasting, in full scale in a large open pit iron mine was conducted to assess the influence of burden on various blast parameters for safe and economical blasting. The paper has described how the full scale tests were performed and how the optimum and critical burden dimensions were determined. The determined optimum and critical burdens were also expressed in terms of bench height and blasthole diameter. Furthermore, the relations established between burden and angle of breakage, volume of broken material, throw and backbreak respectively were given and discussed. The results show that the maximal volume of broken ore was achieved when the burden is almost equal to half the bench height. © 1991, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

entry.dc:title: Practical aspects of availability and reliability management in a large open pit mine
entry.dc:creator: Golosinski T.
entry.prism:publicationName: Reliability Production and Control in Coal Mines Proc International Conference Wollongong 1991
entry.dc:description: The large El Cerrejon coal open pit in north east Colombia has been developed over the last decade in a remote, entirely new mining area with hitherto unskilled inhabitants. Now over 200 pieces of heavy equipment operate with high reliability and availability due to successful theoretical training and skill improvement programs tuned to the specific reliability needs of the worksite and environment. The process of continuous improvement adopted promises further competitive advantages of the project. -Author

entry.dc:title: An application of closed queueing networks theory in truck-shovel systems
entry.dc:creator: Kappas G.
entry.prism:publicationName: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
entry.dc:description: Primary applications of queueing networks theory have been in the area of computer systems and computer communication networks analysis and performance. The application introduced here is a steady state analysis of a generalized truck-shovel system in a typical open pit mine. The service time distributions of each activity are assumed to be of a general form. The approach used here minimizes the error of performance parameter estimates of the most saturated service center. The formulation allows one to obtain estimates of system parameters relatively fast and very close to those obtained by simulation. The relative error of the critical performance parameter estimates as compared to those obtained by simulation do not exceed 5%. The output of the model can be used within various optimization schemes for design and operational control of open pit mining systems. © 1991, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

entry.dc:title: Shallow translational failures along thin marine clay layers at the Syncrude Canada Limited open pit mine
entry.dc:creator: List B.
entry.dc:description: Syncrude Canada Limited operates four 70 cu.m draglines which excavate oil sands from below an operating bench and cast the ore into windrows on the mining bench. Excessive differential settlement of the operating pad and failure of the highwall along thin Marine Clay layers within the Cretaceous Upper McMurray Formation can affect the safety and operation of the draglines. Geotechnical investigation of these Marine Sediments has included site investigations, laboratory testing, the monitoring and documentation of over 200 windrow induced translational failures, full scale field tests, and analysis of piezometric and deformation data from around operating drag-lines. The weak Marine Clay layers and the resultant poor trafficability of the Marine Sands have had a significant detrimental impact on dragline productivity including additional pad preparation time, subexcavations, and dragline downtime to read geotechnical instruments. Studies conducted to date have reduced the negative impact on production, and additional work is in progress to further optimize productivity while ensuring a safe and reliable dragline mining operation.

entry.dc:title: Les Mines Selbaie story: Introduction
entry.dc:creator: Bryce R.
entry.dc:description: Selbaie is located northwest of Joutel in what is known as the fourth east-west volcanic sediment group in northwestern Quebec. The main metals produced are copper and zinc, with important contents of silver and gold. Production comes from an open pit mine on the A-1 zone and from two underground mines on the B zone and the A-2 zone. Production from all sources now exceeds 7000 tonnes per day, with a workforce of 540 regular employees. Of particular interest technically is high recovery of B zone reserves underneath 40 m of overburden cover, low-cost capital development of the A-2 zone, computerized control of open pit mining, and copper-zinc separation of the A-1 zone ore. Due to the low grades of the deposits, efficiency in all aspects of the production process is essential to success of the operation.

entry.dc:title: Les Mines Selbaie story: Open pit mine
entry.dc:creator: Pageau C.
entry.dc:description: The open pit as well as its related services were incorporated into a complex which includes an underground mine and a concentrator. The equipment was chosen with the objective of auto-sufficiency during each phase of mining. The paper outlines the organization and methods used in drilling, blasting, loading, transporting and crushing. The responsibilities of the Engineering Department are also outlined. A short resume of the results obtained as well as suggestions for improvement are provided.

entry.dc:title: Deformation of open pit mine slopes by deep seated toppling
entry.dc:creator: Martin D.
entry.prism:publicationName: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
entry.dc:description: The relationships between engineering geology, structural geology, strength properties and failure mechanisms of several large slope failures in western North America are examined. The main failure mechanism identified at each site involves primarily deep seated toppling, Characteristics, diagnostic features and behaviour of each failure are reviewed, Back analyses of two failures using limit equilibrium techniques as well as numerical modelling confirms that the toppling mechanism is extremely sensitive to mining activity and groundwater pressure, Although deep seated toppling failures may involve more than several million tonnes, large deformations of the order of several tens of metres have been documented without catastrophic failure, These deformations are explained from the results of numerical modelling using a distinct element finite difference code. Ongoing research and documentation of such failures is providing a clearer understanding of the deformation behaviour of high rock slopes. © 1990, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

entry.dc:title: Aznalcollar
entry.dc:creator: Fox K.
entry.dc:description: Located at the eastern-most end of the Iberian pyrite belt, 40 km northwest of Seville, Spain, the Aznalcollar open pit mine has been in operation since 1979. It is currently producing 3.5 Mt/y of complex pyrite and pyroclastic ores from the open pit operation. Aznalcollar is one of the few complex sulphide orebodies being exploited on the pyrite belt to produce separate lead, zinc and copper concentrates. It also produces flotation pyrite as a byproduct and this is sold for sulphuric acid manufacture.

entry.dc:title: Geology of the fushun coalfield, Liaoning Province, People's Republic of China
entry.dc:creator: Johnson E.A.
entry.dc:description: The Fushun coalfield is located in Liaoning Province 45 km east of Shenyang in a relatively small east-west-trending exposure of Mesozoic and Cenozoic rocks surrounded by Precambrian terrane. The coal is included in a sequence of early Tertiary rocks consisting of Paleocene basalt and tuff, and Eocene coal, oil shale and mudstone. These units have been folded into a syncline that plunges gently to the east. The overturned north limb of this fold has been partly removed by a thrust fault. The principal coal beds are low-sulfur subbituminous and bituminous in rank, are of limnic origin, and are contained in the 55-m-thick Eocene Guchengzi Formation. The field, which has been active since the turn of the century, has both open pit and underground mines. The largest operation is the West Open Pit mine, which measures 2.0 km wide, 6.6 km long, and 300 m deep. Coal is mined by means of power shovels, trucks, and an electric rail system. Oil shale from the Eocene Jijuntun Formation is also mined. © 1990.

entry.dc:title: Characterization of overburden soils at Thompson Open Pit Mine
entry.dc:creator: Ramage R.
entry.dc:description: The Thompson Open Pit Mine is currently under development. The North Pit overburden removal program was completed in 1985 and the South Pit overburden removal has been started in 1989 and is currently underway utilizing a suction dredge. Geotechnical investigations were undertaken prior to each overburden removal program to identify the nature and engineering properties of the soils overlying the mineralized bedrock ore zones. Considerable data with respect to soil texture, thicknesses and shear strength was obtained during field investigations and augmented with laboratory testing. Hydrogeological evaluations were undertaken to determine the pore pressure distributions in the overburden soils and to be able to model the existing groundwater regime and the changes to that regime during operation of a dredge and maintenance of a dredge pool.

entry.dc:title: Rampura-Agucha design and development of major lead-zinc project in India. A case history
entry.dc:creator: Jain B.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: A large lead-zinc deposit was discovered during the early 80s at Agucha in Rajasthan in a banded gneissic complex of the Bhilwara Supergroup of Archaean age. Hindustan Zinc Limited began exploration and ore reserves, tonnage and grade were estimated and evaluated. A 3000 tpd open pit mine and beneficiation plant along with other facilities are under development. The project is scheduled to be completed in 1991.

entry.dc:title: Use of the flotation reagent ketgol for flotation of coal from the Neryungrinsk Open Pit Mine
entry.dc:creator: Deberdeev I.K.
entry.prism:publicationName: Coke Chemistry USSR English Translation of Koks I Khimiya
entry.dc:description: The purpose of this study was to investigate the flotation activity of the reagent KETGOL with respect to coal from the Neryungrinsk Open Pit Mine. This new heteropolar reagent is a byproduct from 2-ethylhexanol production by hydroxy synthesis and has found industrial use at a number of coal concentration plants. It is shown that the use of KETGOL offers the possibility of increasing the yield of concentrate by 2.5% with a slight increase in ash content. We should note that the ash content of the floated material at the concentration plant is 16%, and the ash content of the investigated sample was 16.75%. An additional advantage of the reagent is its lower consumption in comparison with diesel fuel and combined feed of reagents is eliminated.

entry.dc:title: Investigation of the feasibility of using coals from the Chernigov open pit mine for production of foundry coke
entry.dc:creator: Zaostrovskii A.
entry.prism:publicationName: Coke Chemistry USSR English Translation of Koks I Khimiya
entry.dc:description: The coals of the Chernigov open pit mine (Volkovskii seam) are arbitrarily classified as grade SS, although according to their main indices they are actually coking coals of grade K2. they are characterized by higher caking properties in comparison with coals from the Sudzhensk Concentration Plant, a higher content of the sum of caking components according to petrographic analysis and reduced ash content (at a mean annual ash content of 8.7%). The yield of volatiles is somewhat higher. Introduction of as much as 40% coals from the Volkoskii seam to the charge of the Kemerovo Plant leads to an increase in yield of volatiles by 1-3.5% and a reduction in ash content by 0.5-1.5%. The caking properties of the charges, characterized by the thickness of the plastic layer Y, lie in the range 12-14 mm, remaining at the level of the similar charge on the average (variant 1). The strength of the lump coke according to index M<inf>40</inf> from charges with participation of coals from the Volkovskii seam of the Chernigov open pit mine increased by 0.03-1%, while the abradability according to index M<inf>10</inf> diminished by an average of 0.5%. The structural strength of the coke declined slightly, obviously because of the increase in porosity of the experimental cokes.
